title: DeWanna Bonner could be the WNBA Finals' biggest X-Factor -- and she took an unlikely path to the Dream - CBS Sports
description: The veteran joined Atlanta just two months ago and is now one of the biggest reasons why the Dream are in the Fin
body:
The veteran joined Atlanta just two months ago and is now one of the biggest reasons why the Dream are in the Finals
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:23 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        SAN FRANCISCO -- Less than two months ago, on Aug. 22, DeWanna Bonner scored 12 points and grabbed nine rebounds for the Phoenix Mercury in a 10-point loss to the Atlanta Dream. By then, the Mercury had long since become the first team since 2008 to miss the playoffs in the season following a Finals appearance. And what may be the final season of the 39-year-old Bonner's storied career was nearing a depressing end. Until, two days later, when the Mercury released Bonner just before the deadline for player playoff eligibility from waivers. Three days after that, on Aug. 27, Bonner signed with the Dream for the remainder of the season. "It happened that Phoenix and her worked out a deal to allow her to make a run in the postseason and that turned into a mini-free agency with a bunch of teams that went after her," Dream general manager Dan Padover said earlier this month. "We were fortunate that we had made a run at her the last few free agencies. She has a great relationship with our players, which helped."Padover took over the Dream's basketball operations in 2022, and over the last four years made five separate trades to acquire all five members of Atlanta's starting lineup: Jordin Canada, Allisha Gray, Rhyne Howard, Naz Hillmon and Angel Reese. That's three All-Stars, last season's Sixth Player of the Year, this season's Defensive Player of the Year and three All-Defensive honorees. 

        
            
                From stunning Angel Reese trade to expansion ingenuity: How Dream, Valkyries broke the mold to reach Finals
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
And yet, without Bonner falling in their lap, the Dream might not be in the Finals for the first time since 2013. "I think she's made a difference both in terms of how good a player she is. She contributes to winning every time she's out there. And I think she has everybody's attention," Dream coach Karl Smesko said Friday after the team's last pre-Finals practice. "She has the right thing to say at the right moment. She's just been a great addition for us as a player and as a leader."
Now in her 17th season, Bonner has won two championships and is the only player in WNBA history to surpass 100 postseason appearances. "She's played more playoff games than I have regular-season games," Dream rookie Isobel Borlase joked. That's underselling it. Bonner's 103 playoff games are more than double Borlase's 44 career games. When Bonner made her debut back in 2009, Borlase wasn't even 5 years old. 
"It's experience, and you can't buy it," Borlase said. "I think the biggest thing for us in the locker room is just her voice. She's a calming voice but also a motivator. She knows when to tell us to pull it together and when to calm down." The rest of the Dream roster had a combined 120 playoff appearances entering this postseason, and Canada and Shatori Walker-Kimbrough, who isn't in the rotation, are the only other players with a ring. "She knows what it takes to win a championship," Gray said. "When DB speaks, you listen." Reese added that Bonner has kept the team "humble" and "grounded," and "told us how important every little detail is gonna be." Bonner, for her part, said that the biggest lesson she's tried to impart is the importance of staying "even keel," especially in a seven-game series. (The Finals were expanded to best-of-seven last season.) "You gotta manage yourself, you gotta manage your emotions, you gotta manage your body," Bonner said. 
Of course, all Bonner's intangibles would mean little without production, and she's playing her best basketball of the season in the playoffs.In Game 1 of the first round against the Washington Mystics, Bonner took over the third quarter to turn an 11-point deficit into 15-point win, and the Dream have never looked back. Bonner has scored in double figures in four of the Dream's five playoff games and put up 23 points in Game 1 of the semifinals against the New York Liberty after Gray went down with a hand injury. She then stepped into the starting lineup for the remainder of the semis and recorded the 20th double-double of her playoff career in the series-clinching Game 3 win. Just look at the splits between Bonner's regular-season numbers and her playoff numbers.

Season10.461.61.140.227.9Playoffs13.26.41.6144.936.8Bonner credited her teammates for making it "easy" for her to come in and assume a leadership role so late in the season. "They accepted it. They're teaching me a lot at the same time," Bonner said. "I'm coming into a team that they've been playing this way all season, so I'm learning as well. We just switch off. They give me a lot of in-game experience and I'm giving them a little bit of knowledge."Together, they could give Atlanta its first ever WNBA championship.

title: Kamario Taylor injury: LSU, Lane Kiffin given layup in CFP chase with star QB doubtful - CBS Sports
description: With Taylor and star RB Fluff Bothwell doubtful, the Tigers have an unexpected break to revive their playoff hope
body:
With Taylor and star RB Fluff Bothwell doubtful, the Tigers have an unexpected break to revive their playoff hopes before brutal matchups against Alabama, Texas and Tennessee
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        If LSU is going to squirm its way back into the College Football Playoff conversation following a 4-2 start and salvage an uninspired start to Lane Kiffin's coaching tenure, it's going to need good fortune and better football.Whether the No. 22 Tigers will play good football when they host No. 16 Mississippi State on Saturday is to be determined, but LSU is undoubtedly beginning the second half of its season with some good fortune. With Bulldogs star quarterback Kamario Taylor and top rusher Fluff Bothwell both listed as doubtful on Friday night's SEC student-athlete availability report, the Tigers appear to have been handed a layup.Taking advantage of it will be critical for a Tigers team that still plays No. 6 Alabama, No. 7 Texas and No. 14 Tennessee. After opening as a 10.5-point favorite amid uncertainty over Taylor's status, the Tigers are now favored by 17. With Mississippi State's breakout star likely to be sidelined by a foot injury that he suffered in a Week 5 loss to Alabama, the Bulldogs have lost their bite.The expected absence of Bothwell will only make life harder on Mississippi State's offense as it potentially navigates life without Taylor, who ranks No. 5 nationally in total offense per game at 321.8 yards.
Turning the page for LSUMississippi State's hobbled status gives the Tigers a great chance to start anew in the second half of the season after road losses to Ole Miss and Kentucky sullied the beginning of Kiffin's highly anticipated first season. While conventional wisdom suggests the Tigers need to win out and finish 10-2 to reach the CFP, there may still be some wiggle room.If the Tigers finish 9-3, they will have an 84.9% chance of reaching the CFP, according to the CBS Sports College Football Playoff Forecaster. In that scenario, they would need to go 5-1 overall and 3-1 against the four teams remaining on their schedule who are currently ranked in the top 20 of the AP poll. Three of those four top-20 games are at home, including Saturday's tilt against Mississippi State.Such an outcome is squarely within the realm of possibility for an LSU team that flashed its high-end potential in dominant victories over the likes of Clemson and Texas A&M. 
Getting to 9-3 or 10-2 will require cleaner play on both sides of the football for LSU. Turnovers have been a recurring issue for the Tigers, who are tied for 117th with 10 giveaways. The defense has been inconsistent, allowing fewer than 200 yards in each of LSU's four wins and 400+ yards in the two losses.But the idea of the Tigers figuring things out in the season's second half isn't outlandish. Flashes of potency have been there, even during its losses. LSU averaged 5.8 yards per play against Kentucky and racked up 26 first downs. The Tigers also scored 17 unanswered on Ole Miss in the second half before faltering late. Where Mississippi State will turnAfter Taylor, Mississippi State's second quarterback is listed as redshirt freshman Parker "Billy" Puckett" or fifth-year player AJ Swann. Puckett, a formerly unranked in-state prospect, has handled second-team snaps for the Bulldogs so far this season, completing 8 of 14 passes for 89 yards.
Swann is a former Vanderbilt starter who spent the 2024 season at LSU before transferring to Appalachian State last year. Now on his fourth school in five years — and third SEC program — he brings some experience to the position.But there's no replacing Taylor, who carried the Bulldogs to a 4-0 start before Mississippi State took a 56-23 loss against Alabama. He appeared to suffer the foot injury late in that defeat. Even after a bye week, it remains an issue.Former Georgia, Arizona State and Sacramento State quarterback Jaden Rashada is also on the Mississippi State roster, though he was not listed on this week's depth chart.

title: Josh Jacobs, Jonathon Cooper to be removed from NFL exempt list, eligible for Week 7 return - CBS Sports
description: Both players will become eligible for Week 7, although their teams must determine whether they are ready to play
body:
Both players will become eligible for Week 7, although their teams must determine whether they are ready to play
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The league announced two players will be removed from the NFL's Commissioner Exempt list in the coming days. Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper will be removed on Friday, and Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs on Monday.Cooper is eligible to play in Denver's Week 7 game against the Arizona Cardinals, and Jacobs is expected to be eligible to play in Green Bay's Week 7 game against the Detroit Lions, according to ESPN. "The league's review of both the Josh Jacobs and Jonathon Cooper situations 'remains ongoing' and is not affected by the change to either player's status," the report states. Players on the commissioner's exempt list continue to be paid. If the NFL later suspends either player, the league could credit the games missed on the exempt list toward the suspension and seek repayment of salary earned during that period. Being on the list means players cannot attend practice or games. 
Cooper was dismissed from minicamp and was placed on the list ahead of the season following two arrests involving an alleged domestic violence incident with his ex-girlfriend in June. He faces five charges, including second-degree felony assault. His trial was moved from mid-November to early March.Cooper has spent his entire career thus far with the Broncos, who drafted him in the seventh round of the 2021 NFL Draft. Jacobs was charged with two misdemeanors, battery and damage to property, from an arrest in May. Jacobs filed an action seeking to prevent the public release of evidence related to the case, including alleged video of the incident. Jacobs' attorney released a statement saying he "accepts responsibility for his actions" and says he is "excited to get back on the field with his teammates."
Jacobs signed a four-year, $48 million deal with the Packers heading into the 2024 season and he is now in his third year with the team. The All-Pro was selected by the Las Vegas Raiders at No. 24 overall in the 2019 NFL Draft.In his absence, RB Marshawn Lloyd has led the team with just 112 rushing yards and two touchdowns. Kaleb Johnson is second on the team with 106 yards. While both players will be eligible to return in Week 7, that decision is ultimately up to the coaches and players involved.

title: Washington QB Demond Williams Jr. to miss game vs. Purdue with rib injury - CBS Sports
description: Junior backup signal caller Elijah Brown will get the start for the Huskies as they look to correct their offenis
body:
Junior backup signal caller Elijah Brown will get the start for the Huskies as they look to correct their offenisve woes against the Boilermakers
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:25 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        With star quarterback Demond Williams Jr. sidelined with a rib injury, junior Elijah Brown will start for Washington against Purdue on Friday night.It's already been a tough season for the Huskies, but this development won't make it any easier. Washington is still looking for its first win in Big Ten play, and that task just got a little more difficult.Brown, a former four-star recruit out of California, played the first two seasons of his career at Stanford before transferring to Washington in the offseason. Brown saw a little action at Stanford and started in a couple of games last season, most notably in a win over Cal and a loss to North Carolina.In nine career appearances with the Cardinal, Brown completed 58.3 percent of his passes for 1,103 yards, six touchdowns and five interceptions. Brown has played in mop-up duty a few times in his first season at Washington, resulting in 276 yards, four touchdowns and zero interceptions on 71.4 percent passing.
Washington needs Brown to spark the passing game because that's been the only way the offense has moved the ball this season. The Huskies rank 16th in the Big Ten with 26.2 points per game, and a pitiful run game has a lot to do with that.Bad news for a struggling offenseAlthough Williams has been somewhat disappointing in 2026, he's still done enough to make plays and put the ball in the end zone on a number of occasions. In other words, Williams has found a way to make it work here and there.The same can't be said for the running game, which has been anemic. The Huskies average just 90.3 rushing yards per game, which ranks 135th out of 138 teams nationall. They also rank 106th in yards per rush (4.06) and rushing success rate (39.7 percent).
That's a bad recipe for a team starting an unproven quarterback on the road in conference play, although there is some hope that Brown has what it takes to lead the offense efficiently.After Williams got hurt against Iowa last week, Brown relatively well in relief. In fact, he started the second half 14-of-16 while leading two straight touchdown drives against the Hawkeyes defense."Just trusting in the process," Brown said of his performance against Iowa. "Just trusting in the coach's plans. I feel like they prepared us very well. That's pretty much it."
Perhaps Brown has taken big strides in his first year at Washington. That would be great, but what if he hasn't? Didn't Dylan Raiola look great against USC when he took over for an injured Dante Moore. One week later, he was benched against UCLA.If Brown does struggle, Washington will go from one-dimensional to zero-dimensional on offense, and even a subpar defense like Purdue's could slow down the Huskies. In that case, Jedd Fisch and and his team would be on their way to a 3-4 record while remaining winless in Big Ten play.

title: Serie A Matchweek 7: Can Inter, AS Roma, Como and Napoli recover after disastrous Champions League week? - CBS Sports
description: All four Italian teams lost in their second game of the league phase in Europe
body:
All four Italian teams lost in their second game of the league phase in Europe
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:16 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Serie A is back this weekend after quite a challenging week of European soccer for the Italian teams, as all four clubs involved in the Champions League lost. Inter, the Serie A leaders, conceded four goals and lost to Club Brugge at San Siro. AS Roma led Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid 3-1 with 10 minutes to go before conceding three goals and losing 4-3 at the Stadio Olimpico on Wednesday. Napoli and Como also lost, so the only Italian wins of the week came from Juventus, AC Milan and Atalanta in the Europa League and Conference League. Let's now take a closer look at what to watch for on Matchday 7: the game, the player and the story you need to know.Game to watch: Juventus vs. LazioLazio have been the most surprising side of the Serie A season so far. Gennaro Gattuso's team is level with Inter at the top of the standings, with 16 points from five wins and a draw in the opening six matches. However, this weekend they will visit Juventus at the Allianz Stadium in Turin. Luciano Spalletti's side hasn't had a great start to the new season, with three wins, two draws and a defeat in its opening six games, and will be looking to react on Sunday after last weekend's draw at Cagliari. Gattuso has shown some encouraging signs following the disappointment of Italy's World Cup playoff elimination against Bosnia and Herzegovina earlier this year. Meanwhile, despite the ongoing boycott of home games by Lazio fans amid their dispute with club owner Claudio Lotito, the Biancocelesti continue to deliver consistent performances week after week.  Player to watch: Marcus ThuramAfter this week's home defeat to Club Brugge in the Champions League, Inter need to react immediately when they visit Bologna on Saturday. Inter coach Cristian Chivu will be without captain Lautaro Martinez for at least three weeks after the Argentinian striker suffered a muscular injury after the Champions League game. He won't be back until after the November international break, so he will also miss the Derby della Madonnina against AC Milan at San Siro on Oct. 31. Inter will now need to rely on their strikers Marcus Thuram, Ange-Yoan Bonny and Francesco Pio Esposito. In particular, the French international needs to step up in this phase to cope with the absence of Lautaro Martinez. It won't be easy by any means, but he's the one who has to make it happen.  Story of the weekend: Italians need a reactionIt was the first time in history that all four Italian teams lost on the same Champions League matchday. That makes it even more important for the four sides that suffered defeats in Europe this week to bounce back in their respective league fixtures. Inter have a challenging away game against Bologna, while Como will meet Fiorentina away as well. Napoli will take on Venezia, who just hired Davide Nicola to replace Giovanni Stroppa, on Saturday, while AS Roma will host their former captain and coach Daniele De Rossi, who is now in charge at Genoa.

title: Allisha Gray injury: Dream star 'making progress,' status for WNBA Finals unclear - CBS Sports
description: Atlanta's title chances may hinge on Gray's availability vs. Golden State
body:
Atlanta's title chances may hinge on Gray's availability vs. Golden State
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        OAKLAND, Calif. -- When the doors at the Sephora Performance Center opened on Friday morning, and media were allowed into the gym to watch the end of the Atlanta Dream's last practice ahead of the 2026 WNBA Finals, star guard Allisha Gray was running through a full-court drill with the starters. While that was a positive sign, Gray's status for Game 1 against the Golden State Valkyries on Saturday remains uncertain due to a hand injury she suffered in the semifinals. Gray, whose 19 points per game led the Dream in scoring and ranked ninth in the league, said after practice that she's still "day-to-day." Dream coach Karl Smesko said a decision on whether Gray will suit up will be made close to tip-off, which is set for 3:30 p.m. ET at Chase Center. "My hand feels good. Today in practice was really my first day of actually being able to have a full practice, go through contact and stuff like that," Gray said. "Right now I'm still day-to-day and then we're gonna see how my finger reacts to how practice went today and we'll see tomorrow."Gray, who still had the pinky and ring fingers on her left shooting hand taped together, said she doesn't think about her finger when she's on the court, and was "just so happy" to be able to "run up and down the court and be able to shoot." She added that the medical staff will ultimately make the final call on whether she'll play. 
"I think she's looking good, making progress," Smesko said. "I don't need to see anything from her. If she's able to go, we'd love for her to go."
Gray recently underwent a "minor" procedure on her left hand after she injured it during Game 1 of the semifinals against the New York Liberty. Specifics regarding her injury and the timing and extent of the procedure remain unclear. Early in that contest in Brooklyn, she deflected a pass from Sabrina Ionescu. After a short trip to the locker room, Gray returned to the game with tape on her fingers. Her first shot was a bad miss from 3-point range, so she removed the tape. In the second quarter, she made another nice defensive play on Ionescu, but aggravated the injury in the process and has not played since. 
Despite Gray's absence, the Dream swept the Liberty in three games to advance to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013. 
Dream's title chances may hinge on Gray's availability"Allisha's one of the best players in the W," Dream coach Karl Smesko said Tuesday. "To advance and beat a great New York team basically without her, except for 10 minutes of one game, is a testament to everybody else raising their game. But it would be great to have her back for the Finals. She's just somebody that, offensively, is really hard to stop, and then she makes defensive plays. She's just an all-around great player."
        
            
                2026 WNBA playoffs bracket: WNBA Finals schedule tweaked so Dream can use larger venue
                
                    Lindsay Gibbs                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Dream's ability to beat the Valkyries and win the first championship in franchise history may hinge on Gray's availability. Jordin Canada, DeWanna Bonner and Isobel Borlase were spectacular in the semifinals against the Liberty, but it's a big ask for them to repeat these performances:
Canada had three of the five-highest playoff scoring performances of her career against the Liberty, and averaged 22.3 points on 62.2/61.5/100 shooting splits -- up from 11.6 points on 43.1/29.2/78.2 shooting in the regular season. Bonner went for 15.3 points and 8.3 rebounds on 50/46.7/80 shooting splits, up from 10.4 points and six rebounds on 40.2/27.9/84.3 shooting between the Phoenix Mercury and Dream in the regular season. And Borlase, who only had six double-digit scoring games in the regular season, came off the bench to chip in 11 points in Game 2 and 10 points in Game 3 while shooting 9 of 15, including 3 of 6 from 3-point range. The Valkyries have the best defense in the league by a wide margin, and just shut down A'ja Wilson and Jackie Young in a sweep of the Las Vegas Aces. Even acknowledging the Valkyries' own issues on offense, it's hard to imagine how the Dream would be able to score enough points to beat them without Gray. While Gray will clearly not be 100% if she suits up, having an All-WNBA-caliber talent on the floor that the Valkyries have to respect would make life far easier for the Dream.

title: NBA Western Conference win totals: Lakers undervalued, Warriors in for a long year - CBS Sports
description: In the 2007-08 NBA season, all eight Western Conference teams won at least 50 games. That will not be the case again this season. There
body:
In the 2007-08 NBA season, all eight Western Conference teams won at least 50 games. That will not be the case again this season. There is a pretty big falloff after the top six West teams (Spurs, Thunder, Nuggets, Timberwolves, Rockets and the Lakers), with the middle class teams looking like the Trail Blazers and Jazz. From there, the lower-tier teams are going to face added struggles of a more competitive nightly schedule, thanks to lottery reform removing the incentive to lose for a third of the league. Factor in how tough the East is (everyone has to play those teams twice), and wins are hard to come by for everyone. It makes picking the over/under win totals an especially difficult exercise, as it is every year. Still, we'll give it our best with the information we have available to us. Earlier this week, we put out our Eastern Conference over-under predictions. Now let's get to the West. 
        
            
                NBA over/under predictions for every Eastern Conference team: Knicks, 76ers overvalued? Raptors ready to rise?
                
                    Brad Botkin                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dallas Mavericks2025-26 record: 26-562026-27 win total: 34.5Prediction: UnderThis is a stay-away line because the Mavericks' season could go so many different ways. They could trade Kyrie Irving and bottom out, relatively speaking, or they could keep Irving, P.J. Washington and Daniel Gafford, get Dereck Lively II back in a timely manner, and with Cooper Flagg profiling as a potential All-NBA player and a bunch of wings and size all over the floor, win north of 40 games pretty easily. 
Deep down, I just don't think Irving makes sense on the team's timeline and they'll ultimately find a way to trade him. And if he goes, why not Washington, Gafford and/or Naji Marshall? I'll go under, but it'll be close. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Denver Nuggets2025-26 record: 54-282026-27 win total: 49.5Prediction: OverAnother tight one. This largely comes down to Aaron Gordon's availability. When he plays, they still kill people. When he's out, much different story. Given that Gordon is healthy right now and has looked good in preseason, I'll give him the benefit of the doubt and err on the side of the Nuggets' pretty much unmatched continuity with its starting lineup. Cameron Johnson caught a lot of flak last year, but look at the numbers. He shot 43% from 3 and was lights out after a terrible start, and he's going to be more comfortable in year two. DeMar DeRozan doesn't seem like a great fit, but he could theoretically help keep the non-Nikola Jokić minutes above water. 
Bottom line, there's still a lot of talent here and one of the best starting fives in the game, and with that at his disposal, I just can't see Jokić not winning 50 games. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
                Golden State Warriors         2025-26 record: 37-452026-27 win total: 37.5Prediction: UnderThis pains me to say as a Northern California native, but Golden State is going under this number. It's always going to be tempting to talk yourself into the idealized version of a Stephen Curry team. Yaxel Lendeborg is going to be awesome! Brandon Williams is going to be a bench spark plug! Gui Santos is slept on! Al Horford can still play! So can Draymond Green!  All we gotta do is keep Curry healthy and stay relevant until Jimmy Butler gets back and take off from there!        Sorry, folks. It ain't happening. The far more realistic scenario is Curry, who only played in 43 games last year and is fighting an old-man knee that seems like it's going to bug him off and on for the rest of his career, misses a lot of time again as the decision comes down to pushing a 38-year-old to his breaking point to maybe sneak into the play-in tourney or erring on the side of keeping his fresh for next year, when they have substantial cap space and are planning (as they always are!) to make a big addition.         
Who knows when or if Kristaps Porzingis will even be able to play. Banking on Butler coming back after a torn ACL and a year off to just be, well, Jimmy Butler in February is a fairy tale. Too many things would have to go perfectly for this to even be a .500 team, and I mean perfectly. It's just not likely. The West is too good, too deep, and the Warriors, frankly, are neither. Take the under.         
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Houston Rockets 2025-26 record: 52-302026-27 win total: 48.5Prediction: OverI don't understand this number. Yeah, the Rockets went in the tank at points last year and looked bad in the playoffs, but they won 52 games with no point guard and Steven Adams, a major part of their major offensive rebounding advantage, out for the entire second half of their schedule. Now the Rockets get Adams and their point guard, Fred VanVleet, back. This is a better team than the one that finished last season with the sixth-best net rating in the league.         If you're waiting on the Kevin Durant decline, get comfortable. The guy averaged 26 points per game last season on damn-near 52/41/87 shooting splits with almost zero structural offensive assistance. To that point, Houston needs to improve its possession quality and find some semblance of dependable late-game offense other than giving the ball to Durant and spectating. VanVleet should help immensely with that aspect.         
Also, don't get too caught up in the lottery-reform narrative as it pertains particularly to the Rockets, who were not a team feasting on tankers last season. Among the top-10 Western Conference teams, only the Clippers lost more games to below-.500 opponents. During an extended December-January stretch, the Rockets lost games to the Jazz, Pelicans, and the Mavericks, Kings and Blazers twice each. They were also 1-7 in overtime games. Chances are, at least half those games swing their way this season.         There's a strong case to be made that 52 wins was about the lowest possible outcome for Houston last season. Based on their point differential, Cleaning The Glass pegged them as an expected 56-win team. And again, they are better this season. This 48.5 number is a comfortable over for me.     
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Los Angeles Clippers2025-26 record: 42-402026-27 win total: 28.5Prediction: UnderThere are some names on this Clippers team, notably Darius Garland and Brandon Ingram. But Ingram has a partially torn Achilles, and there's no telling when he'll be ready to go. 
Max Strus is also hurt to start the year, and the most important factor in this line is that the Clippers almost have to trade some guys to recoup some of the future draft picks they forfeited to the Kawhi Leonard cap-circumvention cause (Rui Hachimura, Kris Dunn, and Derrick Jones Jr. are prime candidates). Ultimately, Ty Lue's coaching might be enough to keep the Clippers out of the bottom-three relegation zone, but they'll still go under this number as they devote most of the season's focus to developing Keaton Wagler. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
                Los Angeles Lakers        2025-26 record: 53-292026-27 win total: 46.5Prediction: OverThe Lakers were looking like a shadow contender until Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves got hurt last year. Yes, they lose maybe the best player ever, but the numbers with Dončić and Reaves on the court without LeBron James still paint a rosy picture.     
With those two on the court without James, the Lakers outscored opponents by 8.3 points per 100 possessions with an 80th percentile offense and defense last season. Rob Pelinka might have paid a bit too much for Walker Kessler, but that's a major addition. If he gets hurt for a significant stretch, the Lakers' defense is shot, but that's the only thing that gives me even brief pause on this number. Assuming Kessler plays in 60-65 games, he will be a possession monster for them on the offensive glass and give Dončić a functional roll partner.     This team is just built to win regular-season games. The postseason is a different story when teams start looking to hunt Dončić and Reaves, but night in and night out, having Dončić and Reaves is such guaranteed high-level offense, it's hard to see the Lakers going under 50 wins, let alone falling down to 46, on the strength of that duo alone with Kessler in the middle.     Now add in some sneaky depth. There are a lot of guys who can catch and shoot 3 off Dončić's gravity. The Lakers can play a pretty mean five-out lineup with Sandro Mamukelashvili at center. Quentin Grimes is a player, and the addition of Collin Sexton maintains creative capacity when Dončić sits and/or misses time. To me, 55-57 wins is in play for the Lakers. Have you forgotten how great Dončić is? This is a wildly low number.     

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Memphis Grizzlies2025-26 record: 25-572026-27 win total: 29.5Prediction: OverI think rookie Cameron Boozer is ready to average 20 and 10 out of the gate. Playing alongside Zach Edey, who was a top-10 offensive board guy as a rookie and is a problem with his size inside (the Grizzlies killed teams in his minutes last year, albeit in almost an irrelevantly small sample as he only played 11 games), he should be able to overpower matchups against smaller defenders. Those two guys and Isaiah Stewart are the frontline foundation of a team that is going to play extremely hard every night. Ty Jerome, who played in just 15 games last year, is very good and will create pick-and-roll offense. Quinten Post gives them size and stretch shooting behind Edey. Cedric Coward, who can really defend and attack the basket with force and has a sweet shooting stroke, is a guy to watch for a big sophomore leap after a strong rookie season. I love Jaylen Wells (in part because I went to the same college as him!). Jerami Grant averaged just under 20 points and shot 39% from 3 on volume last year. I just think Jerome and Edey basically not playing last year and the Grizzlies still winning 25 games (with an incentive to tank) is the profile of a team that can win five more games this season. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota Timberwolves2025-26 record: 49-332026-27 win total: 48.5Prediction: OverShooters convert shots at one of the highest rates in the league off LaMelo Ball passes. He's an extraordinarily gifted passer who hits his in rhythm and on target. Anthony Edwards shot 48% on catch-and-shoot 3s last season. This has the makings of a truly dynamic offensive duo, with Ball relieving some of Edwards' on-ball stress and juice in an offense that, in general, could get a little bogged down running through Julius Randle in the past. You can have your concerns about Ball staying healthy or surviving defensively in a playoff series, but there is a lot of defensive infrastructure in Minnesota with Rudy Gobert and Jaden McDaniels (one of the better true two-way players in the league), and this team is going to play with a lot of energy and swagger. Jonathan Kuminga should really benefit from Ball's hit-ahead passing and general pace pushing. Naz Reid will be missed, and the frontcourt depth could be a pain point. Give me the over. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New Orleans Pelicans2025-26 record: 26-562026-27 win total: 28.5Prediction: UnderZion Williamson is a round peg in a square hole. He doesn't fit next to Derik Queen because neither can shoot nor defend. Williamson needs the ball to really make an impact, but you can't justify not playing through Queen and Jeremiah Fears. 
There are teams that are better than the sum of their parts and teams that are worse than the sum of their parts, and the Pelicans are the latter. They have good players. Herbert Jones. Trey Murphy III. Dejounte Murray. All these guys can play and therefore should be traded because this team, as constructed, is going nowhere and has too many overlapping skill sets with the same flaws. The only question with this team is whether the front office will do the right thing and make some of these trades (notably Murphy III) at a reasonable price, rather than holding out for the Danny Ainge train-heist package. Either way, this team is going under. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Oklahoma City Thunder2025-26 record: 64-182026-27 win total: 62.5Prediction: UnderI'm telling you right now, do not mess with this bet. The Thunder could very easily go over this number. They won 64 last year and Jalen Williams only played 33 games. But in a league this deep, I'm banking on just one 60-win team and it won't be OKC. The Thunder just have the motivation to really put their pedal to the floor. That doesn't matter a ton because their floor is so high, and they have so many deep, guaranteed sources of offense and defense, individually and collectively, but it's just enough of a factor for me to say this team to finish under 63 wins, if only slightly. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
      Phoenix Suns         2025-26 record: 45-372026-27 win total: 40.5Prediction: UnderPhoenix is definitely going to regress from its 45 wins last year. The question is how much? Personally, I think this is a 36-38 win team because they won last year by flat-out playing harder than their opponents.     That won't catch as many teams by surprise this season, and it's just tough to sustain that winning blueprint over multiple seasons when you're at a talent deficit against two-thirds of the league. Lottery reform stands to punish this team considerably, too. The Suns killed the bad teams last year: 23-4 against bottom-10 opponents, per Cleaning the Glass. Those are teams that are no longer incentivized to concede defeat.     Also, can Dillon Brooks really repeat his 2025-26 season? It wasn't the most efficient, but this guy was a flat-out stud second scorer. Maybe he really is that. But a Brooks regression is certainly on the table. Combine all of this with the strength of the West and the league overall, and I just don't see a 40-win roster in Phoenix.  
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Portland Trail Blazers2025-26 record: 42-402026-27 win total: 41.5Prediction: OverI like this over quite a bit. I have the same concerns about the Ja Morant/Damian Lillard pairing as everyone else, but I don't think it'll take Micah Nori -- who's on a one-year contract and doesn't have time to mess around with losing lineups -- long to move Morant to the bench. From there, the upside of his scoring becomes much more of a bonus play. Outside of that concern, I love this team. Lillard feels so right back in this uniform and I have no reason to think he'll be anything less than very good. They'll have to figure out the balance of on-ball creation as Deni Avdija is probably the guy that deserves the most usage and Lillard, though obviously capable, was never the best version of himself off the ball in Milwaukee. Still, we're not talking about a contender here. We're just talking about finishing a little above .500 for a team with a potentially still-elite shot creator Lillard, an All-NBA-level player in Avdija, a top-shelf rim protector in Donovan Clingan, a first-class wing defender in Toumani Camara, and the wing depth of Jrue Holiday, Morant and Scoot Henderson -- who's in a contract year and coming off a pretty quietly solid third season -- to cover for the six-month loss of Shaedon Sharpe, who will be back hopefully for the post-All-Star stretch run. This is a good team unless Morant completely screws it up. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Sacramento Kings2025-26 record: 22-602026-27 win total: 21.5Prediction: UnderThis is the worst team in the league. The 21.5 total reflects that (by far BetMGM's lowest line), but it's not low enough. Darius Acuff Jr. is going to put up a barrelful of empty stats, which will hopefully be a fun reason to watch the Kings, but there isn't a defensive bone to be found on this team. Zach LaVine has to get traded or bought out or something. Domantas Sabonis, too. I mean, this team could very likely be starting Ben Simmons on opening night. If you think they're going over this line just because it's so low, fine. But I can't bring myself to endorse any sort of winning wager on a team this bad. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
                San Antonio Spurs        2025-26 record: 62-202026-27 win total: 59.5Prediction: OverThere's a blueprint for winning 60-plus games. It starts with talent, which, of course, the Spurs are loaded with. Then it's about depth, because guys are going to miss games and winning 60 necessitates putting a high-level NBA team on the floor every night.   And then there's the "something to prove" factor. Victor Wembanyama sets this tone. He openly talks about wanting to win the MVP, so he's going to play the 65 games at least, and he's going to play them hard. Dylan Harper is pushing to prove worthy of all the hype. The Spurs believe they are on the cusp of a dynasty. In the initial stages of championship development, teams like the 2014-15 Warriors and 2024-25 Thunder play the regular season with the fervor of a team announcing the true beginning of its reign. Last season, the Spurs sort of crashed the party. This season, they're throwing the party. They're going to be out to dominate every single night, and with the baseline defense of Wembanyama and so many viable creators that can cover for each other's injuries and/or off nights, the baseline here is just too high with this kind of motivation to see the Spurs going under 60 wins. I think 65-67 wins is the real number. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Utah Jazz2025-26 record: 22-602026-27 win total: 37.5Prediction: OverThe Jazz are finally ready to start playing games with the actual goal of winning. They've traded for Jaren Jackson Jr. and kept Lauri Markkanen all these years. They've seen Keyonte George develop into a lethal weapon. They drafted Darryn Peterson at second overall. And with the spacing this team has with its bigs, those two could combine for 40 a lot of nights. Utah's offense will be very good. The defense is another story. Walker Kessler is gone, and Jackson Jr. is an almost unbelievably poor rebounder for his size. Jusuf Nurkic being out to start the year (listed as a four-week injury, but we'll see) really hurts Utah's rebounding prospects and he is a passer who can tie a lot of this offense together. The bottom line is Utah was competitive in a good amount of games last year until it decided not to be, and there is real talent on this roster. Give me the over as this team fights for a play-in berth.

body:
First place and a potential NWSL Shield clinch are on the line at Audi Field, while Washington fight to lock down a playoff spot in the latest chapter of their fierce rivalry
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:37 pm ET

        It's the best time of the year in NWSL, the playoff push. With just a few games left in the 2026 regular season and the NWSL Shield still up for grabs, every game from here on out feels like a must-win. But, add rivalry to the mix, and the stakes get a little higher.Every great rivalry has iconic moments, and Gotham FC and Washington Spirit have already racked up several in recent years. Washington Spirit won a triumphant penalty shootout at Audi Field in the 2024 NWSL semifinals, and Gotham FC won last year's NWSL Championship game.Earlier this season, Gotham took home bragging rights with a narrow 1-0 win for the first-ever victory at MLB's Citi Field in front of 42,175 fans.
The two teams will meet in a final regular-season fixture, just weeks before the NWSL playoffs begin. But both sides have stakes in the match. Gotham FC already claimed a postseason spot, are in first place, are leading the NWSL Shield race, and can potentially lift the shield. Meanwhile, the Spirit are in third place, still in contention for the shield, and chasing a playoff clinch.
However, both rosters face uncertainty ahead of the game. Injury concerns and cohesion struggles loom, and with the playoffs so close, gamesmanship could flare in a rivalry that's already typically cagey.How to watch Washington Spirit vs. Gotham FC, oddsDate: Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time: 12:30 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: CBS Odds: Washington Spirit +160; Draw +230; NJ/NJ Gotham +155Injury concerns for Gotham FCGotham FC have been on an impressive run of form since the league returned following a summer break for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, with only two losses since July 4. With an unbeaten run through August and more wins in September, the East Coast club has held on firmly to first place. 
Equally impressive has been the club's ability to navigate changes across the sidelines and the roster. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros and his family welcomed a new baby, and he took parental leave back in July."I'm incredibly grateful to everyone at Gotham FC for supporting us unconditionally while we were deciding to take this step," Amoros said in the summer. "This is a personal decision for our family, but I also recognize the visibility that comes with my role. When fathers take parental leave, particularly men in leadership positions, it helps normalize an important principle: Caring for children is a shared responsibility between parents. I need to be there for my family."Between then-acting head coach Shaun Harris and Amoros, the club's record was ten wins, three draws, and two losses through September, and they also had to manage the roster as injuries piled up, with a season-ending torn patellar tendon for Emily Sonnett and a brief concussion precaution for Rose Lavelle. 
The injury list is still growing ahead of Saturday's big game. Rookie Jordynn Dudley's impressive campaign was cut short with a foot fracture, and while on international duty, Brazilian defender Brunhina tore her ACL. Both players are on the season-ending injury list ahead of the weekend. Jaedyn Shaw was recently called up to join USWNT camps with the U23 side, though she was sent home early as a precaution following a minor injury. She is currently day-to-day and expected to be available for Saturday's game against the Spirit.The recent international window may have added minutes for players on national teams; it may have come at a good time for others ahead of a potential NWSL Shield clinch scenario. One of Gotham's strengths this season has been a deep bench that has played together for a few seasons, while rookies stepped up and new additions like Australian international Sam Kerr have slotted in fairly seamlessly following the departure of Esther Gonzalez.
The recent acquisition of Spain defender Leila Ouahabi could mean another tactical shift for Midge Purce, who could play more of an attacking role along the front line, while Ouahabi shifts into a natural position at outside back.Cohesion struggles for Washington SpiritThe Spirit's second half of the season has been more split than Gotham. With eight wins, six losses, and one draw since July, the group has struggled to keep pace for the NWSL Shield, but looks primed for another postseason appearance. Inconsistency in results isn't uncommon in a long NWSL season, and the Spirit shook off a four-game winless streak in August to finally pick up a trio of wins across five matches in September. Roster churn could also help explain some of the unevenness.
Beyond preseason movement, including key midfield departures Croix Bethune (Kansas City Current) and Narumi Miura (Utah Royals) to other playoff-contending teams at the start of the season, the club has made plenty of mid- to late-season roster shakeups. Cameroonian midfielder Monique Ngock and Algerian midfielder Mélissa Bethi joined after the Women's Africa Cup of Nations, and the club recently signed Tanzanian national team forward Clara Luvanga. Mexico international Rebecal Bernal, with 20 appearances for the Spirit this season, joined Manchester United in September. Losing a regular from the squad in the middle of a Shield chase left little time for the defense or midfield to readjust, especially with Leicy Santos out for an extended injury absence. Though there might finally be some light at the end of the long absence tunnel.
Both Andi Sullivan and Ashley Hatch returned to the roster following maternity leave midseason and earned match minutes, and head coach Adrian Gonzalez said in a recent pregame press conference that Santos will be available for selection against Gotham.It's a sign that maybe the international break arrived at a good time for the club's recent signings and injured players. The franchise is investing in international talent, and that's positive for the present and future, but chemistry rarely arrives the moment a new deal is signed. Now that everyone has had a handful of games to get acclimated and a brief international break in the schedule, the Spirit can look ahead to managing the three games remaining in front of them, but first is a high-stakes game against Gotham.What's at stakeThere's plenty to play for on Saturday. Gotham is chasing a prize it has never won. With two NWSL Championships, a Concacaf title, and a recent NWSL Challenge Cup, the title of best team in the league has eluded them. They have a chance to hoist the Shield with a road win over one of their oldest rivals, with help from a North Carolina Courage win.
"There's not a lot of direct talk about it because we all understand that what we're doing every day and every week is what leads to that. So while it's an ultimate goal that we've set from the beginning of preseason, we have a good understanding that thinking about that goal is not necessarily what's going to get you there. It's what you're doing every day at training; it's what you're doing on the weekend playing these games," said Gotham defender Tierna Davidson before the international break."That's really what we're focused on, knowing in the back of our minds that that's what we're working towards together. I also think too, sometimes if you talk about something too much, you forget what's right in front of you. And that's important that we continue to focus on what's in front of us ... ultimately, as a team, we understand that there are short-term goals, midterm goals, long-term goals, but we can accomplish all of that together without having to compromise in any way," she said.The Spirit have the math on their side in the Shield race, but they must beat Gotham and win their remaining games (nine points) to have a shot.
Beyond the shield, there is playoff positioning on the line for both sides. Even if Gotham stumble in their remaining games, the pride of playing for a home playoff is there. Teams that place first through fourth could potentially host up to two home games. Gotham has already clinched a postseason spot, and the Spirit can also cement another postseason berth with a win, or help from positive results by San Diego, Bay FC, or Chicago.

Dylan Raiola will be on the bench against Nebraska as Thomas steps in to see if he can get the Ducks back on track
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:30 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Oregon is turning to third-string quarterback Brock Thomas over Dylan Raiola with its College Football Playoff hopes on the line against Nebraska, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz and Chris Hummer. It will be the first start of Thomas' career.Thomas took the majority of first-team reps in practice throughout the week; he will get his first career start on Saturday. In his mid-week press conference, Ducks coach Dan Lanning explained the factors that went into the quarterback decision with Dante Moore still recovering from a concussion."[Saturday's performance] all plays into effect, and the body of work this week all plays into effect. The question was asked of me why not make the change sooner after the game; I think that's fair. On the same note, I think some of the positions we put [Raiola] in weren't successful opportunities as well," Lanning said. "I think we made some adjustments in getting the ball out a little quicker, creating some more open pictures that allowed Brock to do that. "But you have to be able to protect the ball, that's a part of it, and like I said after the game, Dylan's also a guy that played really well against USC and you have to be aware of that too."
After throwing his second interception -- and completing just 31.6% of his passes -- Raiola was pulled in favor of Thomas against the Bruins. Thomas, a senior and a Eugene native, has been at Oregon since he joined the program as a walk-on in the 2023 recruiting cycle.Despite his age, Thomas has very little game experience. His 15 pass attempts against UCLA make up almost half of his 36 career attempts. In that small sample size, Thomas has completed 72.2% of his throws for 302 yards and two touchdowns.Who is Brock Thomas?Coming out of high school, Thomas was the No. 96 quarterback and No. 10 player out of Oregon in the 2023 recruiting class, per 247Sports. He had scholarship offers from smaller programs like Air Force, Army, Eastern Washington and Portland State.
Instead of accepting one of those offers, Thomas chose to walk on at Oregon, and the Eugene native became a Duck. Thomas has stuck with the team ever since, despite being stuck well behind other quarterbacks like Bo Nix, Dillon Gabriel, Moore and Raiola.Thomas didn't even attempt a pass until September of last year, when he went 0-for-1 in a 66-point win over Oklahoma State.In last week's loss to UCLA, Thomas at least gave his team a chance to win, even if he didn't light the world on fire. The senior made smart decisions in the passing game, which was an upgrade over Raiola, although he did fumble the snap on a key fourth-and-1.
Now, in a surprising turn of events, the quarterback from Eugene will get the chance to lead Oregon to victory after waiting for an opportunity that was never guaranteed. Thomas has the makings of a folk hero if he can seize his opportunity on Saturday.Where it went wrong for RaiolaComing out of Oregon's win over USC, Raiola was heralded as the example of a player who humbled himself and accepted a backup role to reset a career that had been derailed at Nebraska.Two weeks later, Raiola was watching from the bench as Thomas tried to steer Oregon to victory.
Against the Trojans, Raiola looked poised, confident and accurate. He completed 76% of his passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns. In fact, Raiola played so well that there were even faint questions about what Lanning would do if Moore returned from a concussion with Raiola igniting the offense.Unfortunately for Lanning, that dilemma never presented itself. Moore remained out for the UCLA game, and Raiola looked like the player he was toward the end of his time at Nebraska. The junior was careless and inaccurate as he tried to do too much on several key plays.
As poorly as Raiola played against the Bruins, things took a downward turn for him in his second year at Nebraska. Entering college as a five-star recruit, Raiola approached his full potential in Lincoln and broke his fibula, which limited him to nine games last season.
With a rift brewing between Nebraska and Raiola's family, the two sides parted ways, and he landed at Oregon. The USC game looked like a big step in the right direction, but old habits emerged against UCLA. As a result, Raiola will have to wait for another opportunity down the line.Oregon's CFP hopes on life supportThe Ducks entered the season as a national championship favorite, but they've become the nation's biggest disappointment.There's still a tinge of hope for Oregon, but it will probably have to run the table, and this mess at quarterback won't make it any easier. Based on what we've seen out of the Ducks, they can't be trusted to go 7-0 against their remaining schedule.
Oct. 17: vs. NebraskaOct. 24: at IllinoisOct. 31: vs. No. 25 NorthwesternNov. 7: at No. 4 Ohio StateNov. 14: vs. MichiganNov. 20: at Michigan StateNov. 28: vs. WashingtonThere's at least a decent chance Oregon has three losses by Sunday. Nebraska is 5-1 and just took defending national champion Indiana to the wire, albeit in Lincoln.Even if the Ducks go 6-1 with a loss to Ohio State, they'll need a lot of help to get into the playoff field. USC, Nebraska, Northwestern and Michigan would all need strong finishes to make those wins look as good as possible. Maybe that happens, but Oregon doesn't want to put itself at the mercy of the Big Ten's mushy middle.Oregon probably needs Moore back at quarterback this season, which is not a sure thing, in order to have any shot at running the table. For now, though, the Ducks' fate is in the hands of Thomas and an offense that's searching for answers.

title: Nick Saban opposes 24-team College Football Playoff expansion - CBS Sports
description: The former Alabama coach is okay with postseason changes, but wants something different
body:
The former Alabama coach is okay with postseason changes, but wants something different
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:28 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The College Football Playoff is in the process of expanding to 24 teams starting in the 2027 season, much to the chagrin of Nick Saban, who says doubling the number of teams in the current bracket is far too many."I would be for 16 (teams) – I think that would be a good compromise," Saban said Friday on ESPN. "I would be for keeping conference championship games as maybe a play-in for the 16? Which, now, you have 20 teams that have hope. But I don't think there's much support for that. I don't think anybody really likes that."The new format is expected to feature a "19+4+1" model with 19 at-large bids, four reserved for Power Four champions and one for the highest-rated Group of Six champ. Theoretically, that would mean almost every team in the final top 25 rankings would play in the playoff.That also means the likely end of conference championship games. For the SEC, an expanded bracket to 24 teams would need to offset the league's financial losses from losing its title game, which is estimated around $100 million.
"The bottom line is money. That's the bottom line," Saban said "You explained it. Universities need it because of the way we're spending more now for players. There's still a cost to having Olympic sports, which are important, I think to be able to keep and give people opportunities to compete. And how do we do that?"
CBS Sports' Brandon Marcello reported this week the CFP could offer an additional $320 million on top of the current contract.Previously, decision-makers in the Big Ten and the SEC were at a stalemate over future CFP formats. The Big Ten prefers a 24-team field with multiple automatic qualifiers per conference, while the SEC preferred a 16-team "5+11" format. That has since changed according to SEC commissioner Greg Sankey, who said this week at the league's basketball media days a decision on expansion was coming "sooner rather than later" in the coming weeks.
"Attitudes change over time and perspectives change, and so we'll see where that leads us from a final decision standpoint," Sankey said, via The Athletic. "I think in general, we have achieved some of the progress we've expected on scheduling commitments. We'll see if we can finalize those across the nation."

title: Florida trending toward starting Tramell Jones at QB vs. Texas as Aaron Philo deals with injury - CBS Sports
description: The Gators appear ready to turn to their young QB on the road against the Longhorns on Saturday
body:
The Gators appear ready to turn to their young QB on the road against the Longhorns on Saturday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:34 pm ET
                        
                •

        Although Florida quarterback Aaron Philo has been classified as a game-time decision against No. 7 Texas, it's trending toward sophomore Tramell Jones Jr. making his first career start, sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.Philo was injured in the Gators' 38-19 loss to South Carolina last week, and Jones struggled in relief. The sophomore threw for 40 yards and one interception while completing six of his eight pass attempts.That lackluster showing against the Gamecocks aside, Jones has the potential to be a tremendous playmaker for Florida. He was a three-star recruit and the No. 25 quarterback in the 2025 signing class, per 247Sports. Andrew Ivins, the 247Sports Director of Scouting, even compared Jones to Florida legend Chris Leak.Jones received some first-team reps at practice throughout the week, under the assumption that Philo would be unable to play. Coach Jon Sumrall said he was pleased with how Jones responded.
"They're both working hard every day, and Tramell is gonna be ready when his number is called, and he's gonna continue to have opportunities as we move forward," Sumrall said, per 247Sports."I love the way [Jones has] handled himself. Tramell's been great. Philo's been great. At practice today, one of my favorite moments at practice: We're doing some routes-on-air stuff, and, Philo's standing right next to Tramell and Tramell makes a throw and Philo's like, '9, what a great ball. Let's go.' They're there for each other."When Philo followed offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner from Georgia Tech, the assumption was that he would be locked in as the starting quarterback. Philo won the job, but Jones pushed the competition into fall camp after flashing at times in spring practice.
Tough first testIf Florida has its ideal scenario, Jones wouldn't be making his first career start on the road against Texas, which boasts one of the best defenses in the country. The Longhorns have been relentless on that side of the ball, and the numbers show it.They rank 12th nationally in yards allowed per game (264.4), 21st nationally in points allowed per game (16.0), sixth in EPA per play and 15th in success rate (37.9 percent)Yards allowed per game264.4 (12th)Points allowed per game16.0 (21st)EPA per play-0.16 (6th)Success rate37.9% (15th)It all starts up front with Colin Simmons, a future first-round NFL draft pick who leads the country in tackles for loss (12) and sacks (9.5). He has plenty of help in the front seven, thanks to defensive lineman Hero Kanu and linebacker Rasheem Biles.In the secondary, cornerbacks Graceson Littleton and Bo Mascoe can capitalize on any mistake Jones makes if he finds himself under pressure.We've already seen what Texas can do to an inexperienced quarterback once this season. Against Tennessee, the Longhorns sacked Faizon Brandon 10 times and forced two fumbles, although the Volunteers fell on both of them. In that game, Brandon had the advantage of operating the offense at home, a luxury Jones won't have in Darrell K Royal on Saturday.The Gators do have a star running back who could take some heat off Jones, Jadan Baugh, but he's been neutralized in two consecutive games. Florida has to find a way to create more running room for him against a stout Texas front.

title: Dream pairing: How Angel Reese and her new team brought out the best in each other to reach the WNBA Finals - CBS Sports
description: Reese, who could be the first star of her generation to win a WNBA title, has changed her game with the Dream
body:
Reese, who could be the first star of her generation to win a WNBA title, has changed her game with the Dream
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:11 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream currently sit just four games away from being crowned WNBA champions. It would be a franchise-first for the Dream, who joined the WNBA in 2008, and make Reese the first star of her generation to lead her team to a title. Things looked very different for both parties not so long ago.This time last year, then-Chicago Sky forward Angel Reese was sitting at home on her couch, watching the Finals from afar after missing the postseason in her first two years in the league. About 700 miles south in Atlanta, the Dream were in soul-searching mode after the winningest regular season in Dream history ended in a postseason flameout.Reese's two years in Chicago had been marked by phenomenal individual play on the court and a sizeable economic impact to the franchise and community, both of which were often overshadowed by poor team play, perplexing roster decisions, coaching instability and front-office mismanagement. By the end of the 2025 season, when Reese gave an ill-advised on-the-record interview to the Chicago Tribune that threw shade on teammates and leadership (and the Sky responded by suspending her for half of a game), it was clear that the two sides were no longer bringing out the best in one another.
        
            
                2026 WNBA Finals predictions: Expert picks for Valkyries vs. Dream as each team seeks first title
                
                    Lindsay Gibbs                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Meanwhile, the Dream's first year under new head coach Karl Smesko had resulted in 15 more wins than their 2024 campaign and a No. 3 seed and home-court advantage in the playoffs, but the end result was the same as it had been the two years prior: A first-round loss, this time at the hands of an injury-plagued Indiana Fever team. The Dream had All-Stars, but no superstars; they were tough, but lacked a competitive fire; they had a strong culture and core, but did not know how to harness any of that when it mattered the most. 
So, when Reese was traded from the Chicago Sky to the Atlanta Dream on April 6, the match immediately made sense. Reese needed a fresh start, a steady organization and a talented roster. The Dream needed a winner and a fighter -- not to mention one of the best rebounders and defenders in the game."It felt like the right situation for me, and I felt like I was able to come here and help the team in any way I could. Coaches and a GM that really believe in me was something I was really, really wanting after my first two years," Reese said in her introductory press conference.How the Dream made Reese betterBut what turned the pairing from sensible to sensational was what came next. Smesko knew that the skillset Reese came to town with would make the Dream better instantly. But she lacked in one area that Smesko is famous for valuing -- the ability to shoot from the 3-point line. Due to the condensed offseason schedule, a consequence of the late arrival of the new CBA, Smesko didn't have time to feel Reese out, ease her into his system, to see first-hand if the rumors that had always followed her about being a diva or too distracted by off-court endeavors were true. He had to decide right away how much change she could handle. And so Smesko did what he's always done -- he decided to coach Reese hard. And Reese let him.
Right away, he set out to change her shooting motion and push her to take more shots from the 3-point line. He told her that if she made one more 3-pointer every 25 shots, even that would make a difference in how teams guarded her. And then he put her under duress. There was no time for this growth to happen in private; the season would be starting in a few weeks. She was going to have to try new things, and fail at them, in front of everyone."It's really hard for me to not want to rush success. And Karl told me how patient I had to be with it," Reese recalled after the semifinals, when asked about her improvements from outside the arch.Just a couple of days into training camp, in a new city on a new team with new eyes tracking her every move, the players were doing a 3-point drill when Smesko stopped practice and told Reese that she had to make two 3-pointers in a row, in front of everyone, before practice resumed. Everyone had to stop what they were doing and watch Reese try to succeed at the only part of basketball she hadn't yet mastered. 
"I was upset with him that day for sure because I didn't want to let the team down. I didn't want to feel embarrassed of how long it could have took me to make them," she said. "I think you have to understand -- you're at the W level, and we changed her shot, like, completely, and then we asked her to do it in games. And we talked about it," Smesko said. "We said, 'Before the All Star break, you're still going to shoot these open threes. This is how we want you to shoot it. It's not going to be a good percentage. After the All Star break, it's going to start to get better. By the time we get to the end of the season, it'll start to feel really comfortable.'"So you had to go through all those growing pains, and do that in front of everybody. That's the reason why I had her do it in front of her teammates. You're going to have to get comfortable shooting this ball in front of people, and it's brand new to you. It's not comfortable to you."
Smesko was right about the timeline. Before the All-Star break, Reese shot 12% on 3-pointers. After All-Star break, that improved to 25%. In the playoffs? It has improved to 38.5% and been a huge reason why the Dream have not yet lost a game in this postseason."Now it's so easy. My confidence is through the roof," Reese said. "When I shoot them, it just feels like practice. You have those tough times, and you have those tough conversations. But it's a coach that really believes in you, and he knows he knows what's best. And I'm really thankful for him for being able to help me with my career and help me be better for the team. Because I don't think I would be in this situation and thriving as I am individually without him."It won't be easy vs. ValksThe Dream have a tall task ahead of them this series. The Valkyries have home-court advantage, so Reese and co. will start the series on the road in San Francisco on Saturday, and the best defense in the league. But with Reese, the Dream have found their edge and are on a 10-game winning streak. During that span, they've won in blowouts and in tight games, in shootouts and in scrap-fests. And with the Dream, Reese has found the best basketball of her young career, and a place where she can showcase all of her talents and even add some to the mix. The two were a perfect fit, and have worked together to become even greater than the sum of their parts. 
"Just knowing I belong here," Reese said, when asked why she's flourished in Atlanta. "Knowing coming to Atlanta, how much I wanted to help this team and do whatever it takes, not just to get out of the first round, not to just to get out the semis, but to make it to the Finals and win a championship. And the job is not done. We're definitely happy about where we are right now, but we're not satisfied."

title: How Jaedyn Shaw is keeping Gotham's attack afloat in chase for NWSL Shield - CBS Sports

body:
A stingy defense has masked an inefficient offense, but Saturday's showdown against the Spirit will test whether the regular-season leaders have enough firepower for the postseason
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:40 pm ET

            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Is Jaedyn Shaw the one thing keeping Gotham FC's season together? While this may feel like a strange question to pose, for a team that's en route to winning the NWSL Shield for the most points in the regular season, Gotham's stats have been quite odd. As Gotham prepare to travel to face the Washington Spirit on Saturday, it's worth taking a look at those Shield credentials with three games left in the regular season.Unfortunately, there's a chance that we could get an answer to this question during the match. Shaw left United States U-23 international duty with a minor injury and is considered day-to-day at this stage. When asked about her availability for this top-of-the-table clash, Gotham FC head coach Juan Carlos Amoros simply said, "Wait and see." Gotham have conceded the fewest goals in the league while also scoring the 12th-most goals of any team. They have the second-best goal difference due to their defensive play, but when looking deeper at the numbers, they aren't clearly the best team in the league; that's likely the San Diego Wave. By the numbers, the team chasing them has the better goal difference and expected goals difference.
                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Of course, soccer is played on grass and not spreadsheets, but this is important to take note of, with the playoffs around the corner. That xG underperformance on the attacking side of the ball is something that could come back to bite this team, as of the top five scorers this season, four are significantly underperforming their xG. Ester Gonzalez may no longer be with the team, but she was close to hitting her expected numbers with six goals from an xG of 7.85. Sam Kerr has four goals from 9.58 xG, Rose Lavelle has four from 6.26 xG, Jordynn Dudley has four from 5.76 xG, and then there's Shaw. 
How to watch Washington Spirit vs. Gotham FC, oddsDate: Saturday, Oct. 17 | Time: 12:30 p.m. ETLocation: Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.TV: CBS Odds: Washington Spirit +160; Draw +230; NJ/NJ Gotham +155While it was surprising not to see Shaw in the most recent United States women's national team camp facing Spain, Emma Hayes made the point that she wanted Shaw to play consistent minutes with the U-23s rather than come off the bench, given the national team's depth on the wings. That's understandable, but Gotham need Shaw to continue performing at this level, or an attack that is already underperforming will crater on the season. 

                                                                    CBS Sports
                                                            Luckily, there isn't a position that Shaw can't get a shot off from or an area of the pitch that she can't score from. Be it cutting inside from the wing, popping up with a header or just taking a rip from outside the box, she's got you covered. And with so many other stars on this Gotham team, other NWSL sides can't focus on taking away Shaw because then someone else will make them pay.  Despite the inefficiency in attack, the club's defense makes this a strong side, even if it's no longer the true super team Gotham were trying to build in New Jersey. That may even be for the best, as to win the NWSL championship, sides have to be well-rounded and have multiple avenues to create danger, which Gotham have.  That could be enough to win a championship, but if a team can limit Shaw's shots, there are fair questions about what Gotham will do next. Facing the third-placed Washington Spirit will be a good test in that regard, but they're more of a test of Gotham's defense than they are of Gotham's attack. But to win a championship, they'll likely need to go through the Spirit anyway, and with the final set for Audi Field, this is good preparation, making Saturday's clash must-watch TV.
